summary.added_external_crate_count_note: P2-Y1 admits no external crate. academic-competency links academic-domain, academic-knowledge-state, academic-repository-competency, serde and thiserror as product edges, and academic-model-run, academic-policy, academic-repository, academic-repository-analysis, academic-repository-classification, academic-repository-correlation, academic-untrusted-content, serde_json, trybuild and uuid as dev edges, all covered by earlier reviewed receipts, and adds one workspace path package. Nothing links into a product binary that was not already there: the three workspace product edges are path packages this repository already builds, and serde and thiserror were admitted by the phase 1 receipt. Build-time-only additions are zero -- there is no build script, no proc macro beyond serde's and thiserror's, and no code generator.
summary.added_workspace_path_package_note: academic-competency is the P2-Y1 boundary: section 24.1's Competency as an observable performance statement, section 24.3's six evidence stages, and the rule that using a dependency settles no rubric cell. It owns the rendered statement, which has no input field and no constructor; the criterion-to-concept binding the join has as its one key; the many-to-many enabling relation as one stored forward list with two query views; and the two doors a rubric cell may be founded on. It is a separate package from academic-repository-competency because that crate owns what a user did in a repository and this one owns what a user should be able to do, and the direction of the edge is what keeps a promotion constructible without a competency and a filled cell impossible without one.

no_second_vocabulary_note: Section 7.1's node hierarchy was implemented by P2-C1's predicate registry and section 13's evidence rows by P2-N2, and this task adds neither again. NodeType::Competency and PredicateName::EnablesCompetency already exist in academic-domain, so Competency::node_type and Competency::enabling_predicate read that registry rather than declaring a second one, and enabling_qualifiers_are_the_registry_s compares ContributionImportance and Necessity against EnablesCompetency's own closed qualifier schema in both directions. Section 13.2's eight evidence rows are not restated either: PromotingEvidence::of asks EvidenceKind::ceiling and refuses EvidenceCeiling::NoPromotion, so the refusal section 24.3 asks for is that table's own answer. Section 13.2's six promoting rows and section 24.3's six stages are a coincidence of counts and not a correspondence, and this crate builds no map between them: section 13.2's first row is transcript teaching, which is exposure rather than 사용해봄, and section 24.3's 설계 선택 has no row of its own, so a total map would have to invent three of its six answers.

direct_workspace_dependencies.academic-domain: EntityId, which is P2-N1's ontology concept identity and the value P2-N2's admitted evidence carries; and NodeType plus PredicateName, which are section 7.1's node hierarchy and section 7.2's edge registry. A concept reference in the ontology namespace is the registry's own identifier rather than a label, so a criterion naming a concept names the value the ontology issued.
direct_workspace_dependencies.academic-knowledge-state: EligibleEvidence, EvidenceCeiling and EvidenceKind. Section 24.3's dependency sentence is section 13.2's own ceiling read through PromotingEvidence, whose one producer refuses NoPromotion; and EligibleEvidence has one producer of its own, EligibilityOutcome::admit, so evidence that never passed section 13.4's four checks has no representation this crate accepts.
direct_workspace_dependencies.academic-repository-competency: PersonalApplicationClaim and ClaimStanding. P2-R5 separated ProjectSnapshot OBSERVES Concept from User APPLIED Concept into two identities and two provenances; this crate takes the second and has no arm for the first, which no_product_file_names_a_project_observation_claim measures over the whole product source. A claim that has been taken back founds nothing either.

dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-model-run: CalibrationRegistry and its dataset types, to build the fresh calibration P2-R2's OBSERVED rungs require before a finding exists to classify and promote from.
dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-policy: ContentDigest, for the analysis policy hash a P2-R1 snapshot request carries. A product edge in P2-R5 and a test edge here, which is what makes 'this crate mints no identity of its own' a compile error rather than a source scan.
dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-repository: P2-R1's capture_local, SnapshotRequest and the identity types a request carries, so every corpus in the acceptance suite is a frozen snapshot that passed the permission and secret gate rather than a fabricated one.
dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-repository-analysis: P2-R2's EvidenceLadder, Locator, PathClass and analyze, so the corpus's OBSERVED rung is that crate's own judgement and the manifest-only subject reaches the rung below it.
dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-repository-classification: P2-R4's classify and the proof-chain types, so the stances the promotion reads are produced rather than written.
dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-repository-correlation: P2-R3's correlate, which the classification takes as its input.
dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-untrusted-content: SourceIndex, which P2-R1's capture_local returns and P2-R2's AnalysisInput::of checks every unit against.
dev_workspace_dependencies.serde_json: The schema round trip. Section 24.1's six keys are compared against the serialized document, each of the three required parts is removed one at a time, and a hand-written statement is offered in the statement field and refused.
dev_workspace_dependencies.trybuild: The compile-fail suite. Section 24.1's separations are types, and the eight cases under crates/competency/tests/compile_fail assert that each refusal is a program that does not compile with a committed diagnostic -- a sentence handed to declare, a concept turned into a competency and a competency read as a concept, a criterion that names no concept, a project observation claim at the personal door, stage evidence filed under a concept that did not found it, section 13.2's ceiling left unasked, and a filled cell read back out of a document.
dev_workspace_dependencies.uuid: Deterministic UUIDv7-shaped fixture identities, derived from a digest of the fixture's name rather than from a clock. The same helper P2-N2's suite uses.

why_this_dependency_belongs_inside_its_t: academic-competency is a workspace path crate, not an external dependency. It owns section 24.1 and section 24.3, whose whole content is that a competency is a performance somebody could watch rather than a state of a person: there is no statement argument anywhere in the crate, so a `knows X` sentence has nowhere to be written, and Deserialize is try_from and re-renders the statement from the parts, so one cannot ride in through JSON either; declare requires a situation, at least one criterion, at least one enabling concept, and a rubric that witnesses every criterion in both directions, so a competency nobody can check is a value that cannot be built; CompetencyId and ConceptRef have no conversion in either direction and ConceptRef carries the namespace that named it as part of the value, so a P2-R4 classification token spelled exactly as a P2-N1 identifier still resolves to nothing on the ontology side; the enabling relation is one stored forward list with two query views and no reverse row, which is section 7.2's own 반대 edge를 중복 저장하지 않는다; and a rubric cell is settled only by a record whose stage the rubric admits for that criterion and whose concept that criterion names, with no arm that falls back to the competency's enabling set, because PerformanceCriterion::of refuses a criterion that names none. Its dependency set is minimal and the edges it does not have are the point: no academic-store, so nothing here reaches the canonical writer and no migration is added; no academic-worker and no academic-egress-boundary, so nothing in its closure can launch a process or stage a payload.
network_posture: The crate opens no socket, opens no file, reads no clock, declares no foreign function, reads no environment variable, spawns no process, and runs no build script. It spells no std::fs name at all: every artifact arrives as an argument, the way P2-N2's evidence and P2-R5's contributions do. the_competency_crate_touches_no_file_and_no_socket in crates/competency/tests/competency_scans.rs compares the whole set of its use items, the whole set of the two-segment paths it reaches through a crate root -- one, thiserror::Error -- and the whole set of the macros it invokes -- four, format, matches, vec and write -- against pinned inventories in both directions, and runs a whole-identifier pass for fifteen filesystem, clock, process and transport constructs over every file of the package, tests included, with Instant, SystemTime and a bare now among them. every_field_of_this_crate_is_in_the_inventory compares all 55 declared fields against a pinned inventory in both directions, requires each to say which of six things it holds, and refuses a u8 or a u64 in any declared type, so neither a byte buffer nor a clock reading has a name to arrive under; the_unnamed_fields_are_pinned closes the four tuple structs and the three enumerations with unnamed variants that a named-field comparison would miss. Its link closure holds nothing that can open a socket beyond libc, which reaches it through academic-policy's bundled SQLite by way of academic-repository in the dev closure. Every corpus, competency, criterion, rubric and record in its test tree is synthetic and built in process; no real repository is read, no version-control command is run, and no network call is made.
advisory_path: Unchanged. Every external crate academic-competency links was admitted by an earlier receipt and is triaged through that receipt's advisory path. trybuild is a dev dependency already admitted for academic-scenario, academic-desktop, academic-proposal, academic-repository-classification and academic-repository-competency, and uuid is a dev dependency already admitted for academic-knowledge-state. .github/dependabot.yml opens no version-update pull request.
